[[File:David P. Williamson (2003).jpg|thumb|David Paul Williamson]]
'''David Paul Williamson''' is a professor of [[operations research]] at [[Cornell University]],<ref>[https://infosci.cornell.edu/faculty/david-williamson Faculty profile], Cornell University, retrieved 2015-06-07.</ref> and the editor-in-chief of the ''[[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]]''.<ref>[https://www.siam.org/journals/sidma.php ''SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics''] publisher web site, accessed 2015-06-07.</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in 1993 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under the supervision of [[Michel Goemans]],<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=68366}}</ref> and is best known for his work with Goemans on [[approximation algorithm]]s based on [[semidefinite programming]], for which they won the [[Fulkerson Prize]] in 2000.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200009/comm-fulkerson.pdf|title=2000 Fulkerson Prize|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=September 2000|volume=47|issue=9|page=1086}}.</ref> He also received the [[Frederick W. Lanchester Prize]] in 2013. In 2022 he received the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize|AMS Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6893 AMS Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research 2022]</ref>
